verses.1: And after that, Absalom, son of David, had a beautiful sister named Tamar. And Amnon, son of David, loved her.
verses.2: And he created Amnom so that she could begin her journey through Tamar. It was a difficult task, but Amnom was willing to do it.
verses.3: And his enemy’s name was Yonadab, son of Shimeah. He was a wise man.
verses.4: And he said to him, “How can you be so poor, son of the king? Why don’t you tell me why?” He replied, “I am Absalom’s brother. I love him.”
verses.5: And Jehonadab said to him, “Lie down on your bed. Then your father will come to see you. You can say to him, ‘Please come here, my brother. Please take care of me. Make something to eat for me, so that I can eat from it and see what I’ll eat.’”
verses.6: And Amnon lay down. Then the king came to see him. Amnon said to the king, “Please come and see my sister. Let her be shown to you; she has two eyes.”
verses.7: And David sent someone to Tamar’s house, saying, “Please go to your brother Amnon’s house and do whatever you need to do.”
verses.8: And Tamar went to the house of Amnon’s wife. She took the jar, smashed it, and applied the mixture to his eyes. Then she rubbed the mixture into his eyes.
verses.9: And she took the dishes and placed them before him. He ordered that everyone should get down from their seats. And everyone did as he commanded.
verses.10: And Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring me the bride and the bridegroom. Then I will give you what you deserve.” Tamar took the gifts that she had made, and she came before Amnon. Her sister, the bride, was also there.
verses.11: And she went to him to eat. He strengthened her, and said to her, “Come and lie down with me.”
verses.12: And he said to him, “My brother, do not refuse me this request. For such a thing will not be done in Israel. Do not carry out this evil deed.”
verses.13: And I will bear my punishment, and you will become one of the prisoners in Israel. Now, please speak to the king, for I will not be deterred by him.
verses.14: And I didn’t want to hear her voice. So I became stronger than her, and I replied to her. Then I lay down beside her.
verses.15: And Amnon hated her with a great hatred, because the hatred that arises from love for someone who is loved. And he said to her, “Amnon, come with me.”
verses.16: And Al-Odot said to him, “That terrible evil that you did to me by sending me away… I simply couldn’t bear to hear that.”
verses.17: And he called his servant, and said, “Send someone up to me on the roof, and open the door behind it.”
verses.18: And it was covered with patterns, just as the daughters of the king’s wives were also covered with such patterns. Then she was taken out from behind the door, and the door was closed behind her.
verses.19: And Tamar took an iron rod and wrote on it with her own hand the names of those who had killed her. Then she put the rod on her head and went away, crying out in pain.
verses.20: And he said to her, “Abshalom, my brother, your brother-in-law was with you. Now, my brother Hariši is your brother-in-law. Do not harden your heart towards this matter. Return to the house of Abshalom, my brother.”
verses.21: And King David heard all these words, and he was very pleased.
verses.22: And Abshalom did not speak ill of Amnon. He spoke well of him, because Abshalom liked Amnon for the things he did to his sister Tamar.
verses.23: And for some days, they became like slaves to Abshalom. Abshalom was the husband of Achor, who was with Ephraim. Abshalom called out to all the sons of the king.
verses.24: And Abshalom went before the king and said, “Please, let us be made your servants. Please, king, let your servants serve you instead of serving your enemies.”
verses.25: And the king said to Absalom, “My son, let us not go together. Let us not be abandoned by you.” But he refused to go. Then the king blessed him.
verses.26: And Abshalom said, “Please do not go with us, my brother. The king said to him, “Why should I go with you?”
verses.27: And Abshalom burst out in anger, and he sent Amnon and all the sons of the king’s family with him.
verses.28: And Abshalom commanded his sons, “See that you do what is right in Amnon’s eyes.” I said to you, “Kill Amnon! Do not be afraid of him. For I have commanded you to do this; be strong and become men of courage.”
verses.29: And the sons of Abshalom did as Abshalom commanded them. All the sons of the king got up and mounted their horses.
verses.30: And there was a great noise along the road. The news reached David, and he said, “Abshalom has killed all the sons of the king. Not a single one of them has been left alive.”
verses.31: And the king stood up, torn his clothes apart, and lay down on the ground. All his servants also stood up, with their clothes torn in pieces.
verses.32: And Yonadab, son of Shimeah, brother of David, said, “Do not tell the king that all the boys of the king’s household have been killed. They died because of Absalom. From that day on, Absalom ruled over them.”
verses.33: And now, O king’s priest, speak to him these words: All the sons of the king have died, just as if they had died alone.
verses.34: And Abshalom ran away. He covered his eyes with his hands. Then he saw that there were many people walking behind him, from the side of the mountain.
verses.35: And Yonadab said to the king, “Look! The sons of the king have come here as your servant commanded. So it happened.”
verses.36: And as he continued to speak, the sons of the king came forward. They raised their voices and wept. Even the king and all his servants also wept with great emotion.
verses.37: And Absalom ran away, and he went to Talmai, son of Ehud, the king of Geshur. He mourned for his son all those days.
verses.38: And Abshalom fled away. He went away, and there he stayed for three years.
verses.39: David, the king, decided to go to Abishalom. This was because he felt sorry for Amnon, as he had died.
